issues.title: Documented-but-unfixed capacity marker gap makes the key probe fail misleadingly
issues.description: The new docstring records a KNOWN MISLEADING FAILURE: when account B is capped the CLI answers with "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Aug 5, 11am", which `_CAPACITY_FAILURE_MARKERS` does not match (confirmed — the list holds "you've hit your usage", "usage limit", "rate limit", none of which are substrings of that text). So the test does not skip; it fails the ZEPPELIN assertion with a cap message as the "output", indistinguishable at a glance from genuine context loss. The rationale given for leaving it — "the marker list is intentionally left alone here; it is owned by the task that narrowed it" — does not hold for this list: that same helper's own docstring states it is a **local** list deliberately NOT imported from `shared.usage_gate`, so adding a marker has zero blast radius outside this test module. This matters more after this diff, not less, because the docstring now advertises `-m integration` and names this test as the thing that would settle the open question. Suggest adding `'weekly limit'` (and `'session limit'`) to `_CAPACITY_FAILURE_MARKERS`; both are unambiguous capacity signals and neither risks the false-positive-skip the conservative-bias comment guards against.
issues.suggestion: Add 'weekly limit' and 'session limit' to _CAPACITY_FAILURE_MARKERS, and replace the KNOWN MISLEADING FAILURE paragraph with a one-line note that capped-account runs now skip.

issues.title: Reachability guard is existence-only; a contentless transcript still resumes
issues.description: `transcript_exists` only asks whether the file is on disk. The prose above it justifies the guard as preventing a resume into an "effectively EMPTY session", but the empty-file case is exactly the one the guard lets through: the measurement note itself records that a capped account still gets its cap message appended as a transcript record, so a turn-1 cap can produce a present-but-workless transcript that passes the check. The same module already exposes `count_transcript_turns` for precisely this question, and the timeout path uses it (cli_invoke.py:2397). This is a narrowing, not a bug — the resumed session at least still contains the original prompt — but the guard is weaker than the comment claims, and the mismatch between claim and check is the kind of thing that misleads the next reader.
issues.suggestion: Either tighten to a turns-based check via count_transcript_turns, or narrow the comment to state that only the file-absent case is vetoed.

issues.title: ~60-line inconclusive measurement journal embedded in the cap-hit branch
issues.description: The block records a specific CLI build (2.1.220), two run session UUIDs, per-account cap reset dates (Aug 5 / Aug 6, 2026), a VERDICT of INCONCLUSIVE, and a WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT section. This repo does favour heavy inline rationale, but the durable part here is short — 'sessions are local JSONL, so reachability not OAuth identity governs resume; the loop reuses one config_dir on purpose' — and the rest is experiment provenance that is already stale-dated by construction (the account cap dates are meaningless after Aug 6). Sitting inside a hot retry branch it will rot in place and no future reader can tell which sentences still hold.
issues.suggestion: Keep the MECHANISM paragraph and the config_dir-reuse invariant inline; move RUNS / VERDICT / WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT to the task 3454 record or a plans/ note with a one-line pointer.

issues.title: One of the four reason-strings has no log-wording test
issues.description: The delivered feature is 'the cap-hit log names the reason', and three of the four variants get a dedicated wording assertion ('transcript present', 'no session_id', 'transcript unreachable'). The fourth — 'resuming (transcript unchecked — no config dir)' — is the one whose whole point is not making a false claim in the log, yet `test_no_config_dir_resumes_unconditionally` asserts only the resume kwargs, not the message. A future edit could collapse it back to the unqualified 'resuming' with the suite still green.
issues.suggestion: Add a caplog assertion for 'transcript unchecked' to test_no_config_dir_resumes_unconditionally.

verdict.summary: The core change is sound and I verified it: the cap-hit resume branch now vetoes a resume whose transcript is provably absent under a known `config_dir`, falling back to a fresh retry with a rebuilt prompt. It correctly reuses the existing `transcript_exists` helper (already the orchestrator's own `no_transcript` guard at harness.py:2885), scopes the veto narrowly to `config_dir is not None` so the ambient-CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR callers (recon agent_loop, task_curator, taggers, review_checkpoint — none of which pass `config_dir`) are byte-identical to before, and keeps the `resuming`/`fresh` log prefix first so existing greps still match. I grepped for consumers of the old `resume_or_fresh` wording and found none outside the module. `uv run pytest tests/test_cap_retry.py` is 134/134 green, including the 7 new tests, and the new integration-module claim that `addopts = "-m 'not integration'"` deselects it is accurate (shared/pyproject.toml:48). Findings are all non-blocking: one actionable correctness gap the diff documents rather than fixes (the test-local capacity-marker list still misses "weekly limit", so the very probe this task hinges on fails misleadingly when account B is capped), plus three maintainability/coverage nits.
